speaker: Doctor
text: Good morning, I am Dr. Agent. I see you have some skin concerns; could you please describe the appearance of the lesions you are worried about, including their size, color, and any changes you've noticed?

speaker: Patient
text: 62-year-old male. The patient has recently immigrated to the US from Africa and seeks evaluation for a non-healing, red, crusty lesion on the shaft of his penis and a similar lesion on his left middle finger. Previous treatments in his home country for syphilis and eczema have been unsuccessful. The patient is a smoker, with a history of two packs per day for the last 30 years.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for that history. The combination of non-healing, crusted lesions on both your penis and a finger, along with your smoking history and immigration from Africa, is concerning; are these lesions bleeding, painful, or changing in size recently?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Non-healing, crusty, red lesions on the penile shaft and left middle finger. I also have Lesions are painless, History of unsuccessful treatment for syphilis and eczema.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Squamous Cell Carcinoma (penile and acral).

The presentation of non-healing, painless, crusted lesions on the penis and finger in a heavy smoker is highly suspicious for malignancy. I request a biopsy of both lesions to confirm the diagnosis and rule out other etiologies like syphilis or eczema.
